One thing has to be right before any of that applies. A limit order only saves you the spread if it rests on your own side of it. A buy limit written at the offer is marketable: it executes at once, against the offer, at the offer, and pays exactly what a market order would. The saving comes from resting at 50.02 and waiting for somebody to come to you — not from putting a price on an order that crosses anyway. Confusing the two is the commonest way a trader believes they have stopped paying the spread while paying it in full.
